This is where I keep my work for Geospatial Analytics and Applications. Over the term it will fill up with weekly exercises and three larger take-home analyses, covering geospatial data wrangling, thematic mapping, spatial point patterns, spatial autocorrelation, clustering, and geographically weighted models.

Everything here is written in R and Quarto, and the code that produced each figure is visible on the page. I work this way for a practical reason. When an analysis is written up properly, I find out fairly quickly whether I understand the method or only know which function to call, and that gap is much cheaper to discover here than in an exam.

A word on what I am aiming for. Geospatial work makes it unusually easy to produce something that looks convincing and is quietly wrong. A map with the wrong projection still renders. A spatial weights matrix built on the wrong neighbour definition still returns a Moran's I. So alongside the results, I try to record the assumptions each method needs and the checks I ran before trusting the output.

## Hands-on Exercises

::: {.section-lead}
Weekly guided exercises. The goal is to get the mechanics right: reading data correctly, projecting it correctly, and producing a map that is not misleading.
:::

::: {.grid}

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4}
### [Hands-on Ex01](Hands-on_Ex/Hands-on_Ex01/Hands-on_Ex01.qmd)
Geospatial data wrangling with sf and choropleth mapping with tmap. Projections, geoprocessing, and how much a classification scheme changes the story.
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4}
### [Hands-on Ex02](Hands-on_Ex/Hands-on_Ex02/Hands-on_Ex02.qmd)
Spatial point patterns with spatstat. Nearest neighbour tests, kernel density, the G, F, K and L functions, and why the null hypothesis is the hard part.
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4}
### [Hands-on Ex03](Hands-on_Ex/Hands-on_Ex03/Hands-on_Ex03.qmd)
Forest fires in Bangka Belitung across 2023. Spatio-temporal KDE with sparr, the space-time K function with stpp, and what a bootstrap says about bandwidths chosen by rule of thumb.
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4}
### [Hands-on Ex04](Hands-on_Ex/Hands-on_Ex04/Hands-on_Ex04.qmd)
Contiguity, distance and k nearest neighbour weights for Hunan's counties, and four ways to compute a spatial lag of GDP per capita.
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4}
### [Hands-on Ex05](Hands-on_Ex/Hands-on_Ex05/Hands-on_Ex05.qmd)
Moran's I, Geary's C and correlograms for Hunan's GDP per capita, then LISA clusters and Gi* hot and cold spots.
:::
::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4}
### [Hands-on Ex06](Hands-on_Ex/Hands-on_Ex06/Hands-on_Ex06.qmd)
ICT regions for Shan State's 55 townships. Ward clustering first, then SKATER and ClustGeo to see how much homogeneity it costs to keep each region in one piece.
:::
:::

## Take-home Exercises

::: {.section-lead}
The larger pieces of work, where I take a real dataset and carry an analysis from raw files through to a conclusion someone could act on.
:::

::: {.grid}

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4}
### [Take-home Ex01](Take-home_Ex/Take-home_Ex01/Take-home_Ex01.qmd)
Fatal road crashes in the Bangkok Metropolitan Region in 2024, analysed along the OpenStreetMap road network. Network kernel density, network K and G functions, and a Knox test on network distance to tell persistent crash sites from short bursts. The [executive summary](Take-home_Ex/Take-home_Ex01/Take-home_Ex01_slides.qmd) gives the main findings in ten slides.
:::

:::
